item.description: Throughout the month of August, the works of artist Michael Alemayehu are on display at Deer Park branch . Michael Alemayehu is a self-taught Ethiopian artist based in Canada. Through graphite and colored pencils, he creates realistic portraits and wildlife art. His work reflects his heritage and passion for detail, inviting viewers to see the beauty of Africa and beyond. "Art has always been my language of expression and connection. Inspired by my Ethiopian roots, I use realism to honor culture, identity, and nature. With every drawing, I aim to spark fascination and share stories that celebrate beauty and tradition." This exhibit is part of TPL's Art Exhibit Space program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods. The exhibit can be viewed during Deer Park's open hours. item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Fatyma Khan — Sun Aug 2, 12:00 AM — North York Central Library
item.description: Throughout the month of August, works by artist Fatyma Khan are on display at North York Central Library branch. Fatyma Khan is an award-winning abstract art photographer based in Toronto. Fatyma Khan's work delves into the intricate relationship between individuals and their environments, emphasizing textural composition and the evocative study of light. Fatyma’s photography is marked by a contemplative approach, capturing the emotional and psychological landscapes shaped by spatial context. Her images often reflect the subtle tension between inner experience and outward reality, offering viewers a space to engage with the layered complexities of perception, presence, and place. This exhibit is part of TPL's Art Exhibits Space program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. item.description: Throughout the month of August, the works of Vytik Art Collective are on display at Northern District Library. Vytik Art Collective is a group of emerging visual artists and curators exploring contemporary art in Toronto. Founded in 2023, it began as a platform for Ukrainian newcomer artists to connect, collaborate, and become part of Canada's art community. In just two years, Vytik has grown into a diverse collective of artists from different cultural and professional backgrounds, creating new ways to make and experience art. "Intersections" Film & Digital Photography Exhibition brings together 20 emerging and established photographers who express their unique perspectives on urban landscapes through architecture, streets, lines, movement, and everyday moments of city life: Alexey Makhinko, Anastasia Skrypnyk, Ava Tsarynnyk, Evan Rajkovic, Gabriel Waddington, Hadi Amtaeleq, Jason Hong, Joshua Kennington, Kyle Alialy, Mariia Charuta, Mark Krzepis, Marta Kolotylo, Nicola Jekubik, Pedro

item.title: Colson Whitehead: Cool Machine — Wed Aug 5, 7:00 PM — Toronto Reference Library
item.description: Two-time Pulitzer Prize-winner Colson Whitehead discusses the magnificent final volume of his Harlem Trilogy. Cool Machine returns us to the world of successful business owner/master fence Ray Carney as he gambles on one last heist to support his beloved wife, but finds himself entangled with a legendary criminal mastermind. Still haunted by his inability to save his cousin Freddie years earlier, Carney comes out of retirement to team up with friend and partner in crime, Pepper, for a chance to rescue Freddie’s son from the violent forces of the city, even if it means risking the safety and security he’s spent decades building for his family. With his trademark pitch-perfect prose, Whitehead magnificently brings to life 1980s New York, painting a portrait of a city and a family in transition. item.title: Basic Woodworking with Marc Reeve-Newson — Sun Aug 9, 10:00 AM
item.description:
If you're afraid of any of the big, loud, finger-severing tools downstairs this is your chance to learn to use them safely.
If you’re afraid of any of the big, loud, finger-severing tools downstairs this is your chance to learn to use them safely and make something practical at the same time. The goal of the class is to learn how to use common power tools and explore basic woodworking joints (mitre, rabbet, and dado). Your end goal is to create a lidded box with internal dimensions of 3″ x 3″ x 4″ that you’ll be able to cherish forever (or hide in shame, but hey, the point of the class is to learn the tools). We’ll start by learning how to use the planer and jointer to take a piece of rough lumber and turn it into a usable board. You’ll then use the table saw, chop saw, and router to shape those pieces, and finally the brad nailer, clamps, and glue to put it all together. If there’s enough time you’ll be able to sand down your creation, add some detailing with the router, and oil it.

item.title: DAX agéntico: valida, genera y optimiza medidas con agentes de IA — Mon Aug 10, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto El DAX siempre ha sido la barrera de entrada a Power BI para muchos profesionales.
En esta sesión veremos cómo los agentes conectados al Remote MCP Server usan el mismo motor de generación DAX que Copilot para Power BI, y cómo el Local MCP permite validar y ejecutar consultas DAX directamente contra el modelo para testear medidas, depurar cálculos y explorar datos sin salir del agente.
Exploraremos prompts avanzados para generar medidas complejas, patrones de inteligencia de tiempo, cálculos condicionales y medidas de tabla, y veremos los límites actuales — qué tipos de DAX generan bien los agentes y dónde todavía hay que revisar.
También cubriremos cómo optimizar el modelo semántico para mejorar la calidad de generación DAX por parte del agente, y cómo combinar Local y Remote MCP en el mismo flujo de trabajo.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto
